summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of bank holidays in India, their impact on financial transactions, and the role of digital banking, with most claims being accurate or consistent with official information.

claims.claim: Banks across India, including major players like SBI and HDFC, will observe several holidays between July 13 and July 19, 2026.
claims.note: Banks will be closed for four days between July 13 and July 19, 2026, including weekend holidays and some state-specific holidays.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) publishes a comprehensive calendar of bank holidays for public reference.
claims.note: The RBI announces bank holidays, including weekends and regional festivals, and publishes a comprehensive calendar.

claims.claim: Bank holidays in India are categorised and notified by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
claims.note: RBI decides bank holidays in three categories, including 'Holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act'. The power to declare public holidays under this Act was delegated to state governments.

claims.claim: While digital fund transfer systems like NEFT and RTGS operate 24/7, 365 days a year, the final settlement and credit to the beneficiary's account might see minor delays if the receiving bank's internal systems require manual intervention on a holiday, though this is rare for fully automated systems.
claims.note: NEFT and RTGS operate 24x7, 365 days a year.

claims.claim: If you deposit a cheque on a bank holiday, its processing will only begin on the next working day. This can delay the crediting of funds to your account.
claims.note: Under Section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, if the maturity date of a promissory note or bill of exchange falls on a public holiday, it is deemed due on the preceding business day.

article_title: Bank Holidays in July: Plan Your Finances Around Upcoming Closures
